I've been farming this same land since I was twenty. My father farmed here before me. I know Quzhou soil — it's heavy loam, decent enough if you water it right and don't skimp on fertilizer.

Seven mu is small. My son works in Baoding now, so during busy seasons it's mostly me and my wife. I can't afford experiments. I do what works.

**Wheat (October planting):** I'll use Jimai seed — everyone in the village uses it, yields are reliable. I rotary till after the maize harvest, work in compound fertilizer before seeding. Then I come back with urea at jointing. Three irrigations: one before winter sets in, one at jointing, one at heading. In spring I spray herbicide when the weeds come up, then fungicide before heading because powdery mildew is bad some years here. I expect around 450 jin per mu if the spring isn't too dry.

**Maize (June planting):** Right after wheat harvest I plant hybrid seed — Zhengdan or Xianyu, whatever the seed shop has. No deep tillage, just direct seeding, saves time and my back. I put compound fertilizer in at planting, then chase it with urea at big bell stage when the plant needs it most. One irrigation at tasseling if the summer is dry like last year. Herbicide right after emergence. I should get 550 jin per mu or more — maize is easier than wheat.
